objects.original: A real-valued function and its Euclidean gradient.
objects.reconstructed: A real-valued function and the Riesz gradient of its Frechet derivative.
objects.evidence: For E equal to Euclidean d-space the Riesz vector is precisely the ordinary gradient. ContDiff ensures this is an actual derivative, not an arbitrary vector field.

domains.reconstructed: All of any complete real inner-product space E.
domains.evidence: The module-scoped CompleteSpace and InnerProductSpace instances permit infinite dimension. Euclidean specialization is supported, but the unrestricted statements are not identical. All-space convexity is retained; a constrained-domain version is not certified.

quantifiers.original: Each admissible f and modulus, with the model and conclusion holding for every ordered pair x,y.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Each admissible E,f,modulus; the upper model and bound are global in x,y.
quantifiers.evidence: No minimizer, exceptional set, bounded ball, or point-dependent constant appears. LipschitzWith packages exactly the universal pairwise norm estimate.

assumptions.original: Convex C1 function with the global quadratic upper model at a nonnegative modulus.
assumptions.reconstructed: ContDiff real 1, ConvexOn univ, the same quadratic upper model; strictly positive real beta.
assumptions.evidence: Definition 1.12 supplies C1 and beta>=0; Exercise 3.1 explicitly removes the section-wide C2 convention. Beta>0 restricts this declaration to the reciprocal formula's positive-denominator domain; it does not settle a reciprocal expression at zero.

conclusion.reconstructed: Squared gradient difference <= 2 beta times the Bregman gap.
conclusion.evidence: Multiplication/division by 2 beta preserves order only for beta>0; exactly on that domain, the coefficients and endpoint orientation agree.

scopes.original: Exercise 3.1, with its individual Bregman/cocoercivity/Lipschitz obligations.
scopes.evidence: The full module carries three declarations, but this binding claims only its named obligation. Acceptance is restricted to Euclidean specialization with beta>0, plus explicitly identified Hilbert generalization; no zero-denominator theorem or whole-exercise identity is claimed.

constant_dependencies.original: Coefficient 1/(2 beta), using smoothness coefficient beta/2.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Coefficient 2 beta after clearing the denominator.
constant_dependencies.evidence: No dimension, norm-equivalence factor, f-dependent auxiliary constant, or regularity constant is introduced. The trial step is beta inverse; its positivity is explicitly assumed.

deltas.description: The formal theorem generalizes Euclidean space to a real Hilbert space.
deltas.evidence: Module-scoped E is complete and inner-product, with no finite-dimensional assumption. Publication assumptions disclose this; source support is by Euclidean specialization, not identity of unrestricted domains.

deltas.description: The Bregman declaration is restricted to beta>0.
deltas.evidence: Definition 1.12 permits zero but (3.4) uses 1/(2 beta). The lesson and bregman-positive-domain binding correctly limit this proof edge. No separately reviewed repaired source statement is supplied or accepted.

source_review.evidence: The packet-bound module uses convex first-order support at x and z=y-beta^-1 d, then the upper model from y to z. Subtraction leaves B_f(y,x)-||d||^2/(2 beta)>=0. The lesson explains the same elimination of f(z), sign, trial point and positive denominator. It cites the actual supporting-plane ASTIS call and separates Mathlib calls from external provenance. Accepted only for the stated binding and Euclidean specialization; generalization and positive-domain limitations above remain explicit.
